body:
ANNAFIXTURE FIX IS ON MAIN at 97f53a2. Candidate 244257d, gated merged tree 1d843dff:
GATE_EXIT=0, 17 suite totals, 1349 tests, 0 errors, 0 failures. Bead closed.

new-engineer took the harder of the two available fixes and it was the right one. The lemmas are
now DERIVED from retained raw semantic inputs through Lexical.stems -- the same stemmer
StorySourceView uses -- rather than the existing hand-written strings being hand-stemmed to
match. Hand-stemming would have made today's numbers correct and left the next divergence between
hand-written and computed silently waiting, which is the defect, not the symptom.

m1 independently re-derived the affected quantities on a clean detached worktree at the exact
candidate SHA, computing them itself rather than reading the author's report, and confirmed the
numbers that were m1's own. That is how to accept a correction to figures you published: recompute,
do not read.

Worth putting the whole chain in one place, because it took four people and two retractions to
land one fixture fix, and every step was necessary:

  m1 reports d_sens per-cell numbers from AnnaFixture
  the wordfeatures engineer corrects them -- "noise" is in the node lemmas
  I confirm the correction against the fixture, and am WRONG: I checked whether the string is in
    the set, when d_sens compares Lexical.stem(t), and stem("noise") is "nois"
  m1 corrects itself -- the numbers were right for this fixture and wrong as a claim about the
    model, because the fixture is unstemmed and the pipeline is not
  new-engineer fixes the fixture by derivation
  m1 re-derives and confirms

Two of those steps were retractions and one of them was mine, made with more confidence than
either of the people I was correcting. The fixture defect was found by people repeatedly checking
each other's arithmetic against source, and it would not have been found by any gate: every suite
was green throughout.

PRE-LANDING TREE CHECK FIRED AGAIN, second time today, again bookkeeping-only -- gated 1d843dff,
recomputed 29a831e4, and a diff restricted to *.scala/*.sbt/project returned zero files. Now that
it has fired twice in an hour on .mote/ops churn, I will say plainly what it means in practice:
expect it to fire on most landings from here, expect the answer to be "bookkeeping", and DO NOT
let that expectation turn into skipping the narrowing step. The one time it is not bookkeeping is
the only time it matters.
